SPEC: Length=288.06km and Diameter=24in are an exact, high-precision match to SNGPL's own official current network data -- as strong a spec confirmation as this project gets, short of a second fully independent (non-SNGPL) source. concerns.researcher_notes: The recorded Status='construction' with StartYear1=2025 looks stale/wrong, not just unsourced. SNGPL's own FY2025 Annual Report (sngpl.com.pk/download/AnnualReport-2025/SNGPLAR2025.pdf), on its p.76 'Milestones' page (a historical-achievements timeline, NOT a future-plans page — confirmed by the table of contents entry '76 Milestones' and by every other entry on that page being past-tense completed work), lists 'PROJECT X (PHASE III): 16"-42" dia x 762 KM long Qadirpur–Lahore Pipeline along with installation of 25,000 HP Compression [to transport] gas downstream Sawan up to Lahore' as a completed item, immediately adjacent to 'PROJECT X (PHASE IV): 30"/24" dia x 149 KM long spurs...for supply of RLNG to Power Plants i.e. Bhikki, Balloki, Haveli Bahadur Shah and Nandipur' (also completed). This matches GEM's P3178 almost exactly on route (Sawan/Qadirpur→Lahore), diameter ceiling (42in), and stated purpose (RLNG transport downstream of Sawan) — GEM's 770km sits inside the 750–780km band every source uses for this same corridor (see the confirmed-caveat entry below). Independently, nsenergybusiness.com's Bhikki power-plant page states the plant's RLNG 'is supplied...through an 18km spur gas pipeline connected with SNGPL's Qilla Sattar Shah to Bhikki pipeline' — Qilla Sattar Shah near Lahore is the exact terminus named in the original 2017 sanction press (offshore-energy.biz: '42-inch pipeline from Sawan to Qilla Satar Shah, near Lahore (780km)'), confirming that trunk is built and live. Further independently, Dawn (dawn.com/news/1368494, Nov 2017) reports LNG-terminal maintenance forcing supply curtailments to Bhikki, Haveli Bahadur Shah, Balloki and Nandipur ('85MMCFD is being supplied to Balloki, Nandipur-31MMCFD' etc.) — i.e. these plants were already drawing RLNG through this network by November 2017, years before GEM's recorded 2025 start. Three independent, non-GEM sources (SNGPL's own corporate report, an industry trade outlet, and a national newspaper) converge on the same conclusion: the trunk is built and has been moving RLNG since 2017–18, not 'under construction' toward a still-future 2025 start. Filed as a spec/status concern rather than existence — the pipeline unquestionably exists; what's wrong is the lifecycle stage recorded for it. Full sourcing/verdict in the status_reviews array below (do not also treat this as a fill for Status[ref] or Start[ref] — those are marked UNRESOLVED, not confirmed, since I am NOT supporting the current values).

GEM's recorded SegmentCost of $672,000,000 implies an effective rate of ~PKR164/USD, which is a mid-2022/2023-era rate, not a 2017 one. This looks like a currency-conversion-year mismatch (the PKR figure converted at a much-later, post-devaluation rate rather than the rate contemporaneous with the 2017 sanction), the same class of defect already logged elsewhere in this project as a length-units/exchange-rate hazard. I could not find an independent, more recent PKR figure that would justify $672M as a genuinely lower re-estimated cost (no cost-overrun-reduction or re-scoping story turned up), so I'm not proposing a replacement number — just flagging the number as unreconciled and worth a human re-check of the original entry's conversion math. concerns.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) on WebFetch, and wiki_citations.json is empty for this row per the scope note, so there were no sheet-cited sources to re-check -- this was ground-up open-web research. The row's [ref] set was completely empty (all 8 units MISSING_REF), so the first question was existence: is 'HQ2-Tando Adam Gas Pipeline' a real, independently-documented SSGC line, or a GEM-only/hallucinated entity? It is real. Two independent Government of Pakistan documents name this exact segment: (1) the Ministry of Energy Petroleum Division / PPIS 'Investment Brochure' gas-transmission-network schematic map (ppisonline.com), which labels a segment '24"x81KM HQ2-TANDO ADAM SECTION' -- diameter and length match GEM's 24 in / 81 km exactly; (2) OGRA's 'State of [the] Regulated Industry' report, Table 3.21 'SSGCL's Capacity Utilization of Transmission Network' (source cited in the report as SSGCL), which lists a row '24'' Dia.X 84 Km HQ2-TandoAdam' with Available Capacity of 85 MMCFD as of both June 30 2019 and June 30 2020 -- capacity matches GEM's 85.00 MMcf/d exactly, diameter matches (24 in), but length is stated as 84 km, not 81 km. This is a genuine cross-source disagreement (81 vs 84 km, ~3.6%), not a GEM error vs. a single correct source -- I found no third source to break the tie, so I'm flagging rather than silently keeping GEM's 81 km. Both documents also confirm classification (OGRA's table sits under section 3.3.3 'SSGCL Transmission infrastructure' / heading 'NATURAL GAS', i.e. this is unambiguously a gas transmission segment, matching GEM's PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas) and ownership (OGRA table explicitly sourced '(Source: SSGCL)' i.e. Sui Southern Gas Company, matching GEM's Owner1=Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100%). Status=operating is inferred from context, not a literal statement: the OGRA table reports nonzero Available Capacity for this named segment in two consecutive fiscal years (FY19, FY20), i.e. it is treated as a live, in-service part of SSGCL's transmission network in that regulatory filing (the report separately notes segment-level utilization % 'could not be calculated due to integrated transmission network', so I did not try to force a literal utilization figure). No duplicate risk within the 63-row roster: the two OGRA-table neighbours 'Masu-HQ3' (24"x15km, cap 40) and the 'Tando Adam to Masu' loopline (24"x34km, cap 23) are genuinely distinct adjoining SSGC segments, and neither appears elsewhere in the roster under another name, so P4017 is not a relabel of another tracked row. Minor attribution caveat (not escalated to its own concern): GEM's StartLocation is 'Nawabshah', but the segment's actual named origin per both sources is the 'HQ2' station/node, not the town of Nawabshah itself -- on the PPIS schematic, HQ2 sits in the same corridor cluster as a '...N.Shah-...NAWABSHAH' label (alongside other HQ2-linked segments: 42"x82km Nara-HQ2, 24"x16km HQ2-KA, 42"x50km Lundo HQ2-Nara), which is consistent with GEM's town-level simplification but is not a literal confirmation that HQ2 is coincident with Nawabshah town proper; EndLocation='Tando Adam' is solidly confirmed since it's literally in the segment's name in both sources.

concerns.recommendation: Re-verify Length (and implicitly Diameter/RouteAccuracy) against SSGC/SNGPL network documentation. The only independent primary source found for this corridor (Business Recorder, 2004-12-25, 'SNGPL and SSGC sign agreement for gas transportation') describes SSGC providing SNGPL ~270 km (168 miles) of existing pipe ('ILBP') from Nawabshah (Sindh) to a compression station at Sui (Balochistan) to carry gas purchased from Hassan field -- and it names that corridor 'Nawabshah-Sui', not 'Hassan-Sui'. GEM's row records Length=58 km / Diameter=16in for a segment called 'Hassan-Sui'. 58 km vs 270 km is not a units/rounding artifact (ratio ~4.7x, not a clean mi/km conversion). Two readings are possible: (a) there is a genuinely distinct, short (~58 km is geographically plausible: Hassan field sits in the Shikarpur/Sukkur/Jacobabad triangle of upper Sindh, and straight-line distance from that area to Sui, Balochistan is roughly 60-90 km) dedicated field-gathering/tie-in spur from Hassan field itself to the Sui hub, separate from the 270 km Nawabshah bypass line used for onward wheeling to SNGPL's Punjab network; or (b) GEM's row is a mislabeled/garbled representation of the Nawabshah-Sui wheeling arrangement with an incorrect length carried over. I could not independently confirm scenario (a) with any source -- no SSGC network map, OGRA report, or news piece describing a dedicated 58 km/16in 'Hassan-Sui' line was found. Do NOT delete the row on this basis (the underlying commercial gas-transport arrangement from Hassan field via Sui is well corroborated -- see below), but the Length/Diameter values need a source before they should be treated as confirmed; consider whether this row should instead represent the 270 km Nawabshah-Sui segment (with RouteAccuracy corrected) or be reconciled against whatever GEM intended.

CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is directly supported by Brecorder's own language ('transmission capacity of 30 mmcfd'), so no classification concern. concerns.researcher_notes: Existence and ownership/classification are corroborated (see the paired confirmed-caveat entry), but I could NOT independently corroborate the SPECIFIC recorded spec (LengthKnown=76.67 km, Diameter=16in uniform, StartLocation=Sahiwal / EndLocation=Lahore) against any single documented SNGPL segment -- and there is a real numeric red flag. P4108 'Sahiwal-Lahore Gas Pipeline I' (same nominal endpoints) is 142.93 km; P4140 'Pipeline-II' is only 76.67 km -- roughly HALF the length for a supposedly parallel line between the same two cities (Sahiwal to Lahore is itself ~130-140 km by road/pipe corridor, matching P4108, not P4140). Searching SNGPL's own Annual Report 2022 (Note 20.1.4 and the infrastructure-projects section, both read via pdftotext after downloading the live PDF -- gem.wiki/anonymous search engines were not usable this run, WebSearch budget was exhausted, and ogra.org.pk/duckduckgo/google/bing all blocked automated fetches, so I worked from SNGPL's and the Wayback-hosted OGRA PDF directly) turned up two candidate real segments in the right length range but NEITHER matches P4140 cleanly: (a) 'Sahiwal - Phool Nagar (1st Segment)', 24in dia, 67.77 km (differs from P4140 by ~9 km AND by diameter, 24in vs 16in); (b) the FY2021-22-completed pair '24in dia x 46.80 km Phoolnagar to Nabi Bakshwala (Ferozepur Road)' + '16in dia x 26.20 km Ferozepur Road to Barki (Phase-I)', which sum to 73.0 km (within ~5% of P4140's 76.67 km) but are explicitly a Lahore-CITY network augmentation/bifurcation project starting at Phool Nagar (a town roughly 35-45 km from Lahore), not a long-haul Sahiwal-origin trunk line, and are two different diameters (24in + 16in), not a single uniform 16in run. Phool Nagar sits geographically between Sahiwal and Lahore on this corridor, so it is plausible GEM's 'Sahiwal-Lahore Gas Pipeline-II' is actually this Phoolnagar-ward segment mislabeled with Sahiwal as the nominal corridor start (the roster itself sets precedent for looplines starting at an intermediate point while keeping the corridor's full name, e.g. P4097/P4098 'Sui-Multan Gas Loopline II/III' both actually list StartLocation=Bhong, not Sui) -- but here GEM lists StartLocation=Sahiwal for P4140, not Phool Nagar, which is the opposite of that established pattern and is itself suspicious. I do not have a source naming '76.67 km' or a uniform '16in Sahiwal-Lahore' pipe verbatim, so per the corroboration standard (a source must AGREE with the GEM number, not merely mention the pipeline) this is a material, unresolved disagreement -- flagging spec/attribution rather than silently passing it. Did not find any evidence the row is fabricated (existence of transmission pipe on this corridor, and of a distinct 'II'-generation pipeline, is well supported) so this is a spec/attribution concern, not an existence concern.

concerns.recommendation: Do not delete or fabricate a corrected number — but flag Diameter=16in for a targeted follow-up. On SNGPL's own map, the segments that literally run Dakhni -> Meyal Plant -> Dhulian (the route matching GEM's title) are labelled 8in (Dakhni link), 24in (Dakhni-Meyal Plant), and 18in (Meyal Plant-Dhulian mainline) - NOT 16in. concerns.researcher_notes: Full detail: I fetched and visually read SNGPL's official Transmission Network map (dated AS ON 30-06-2026, images/transmission/TransmissionMap072026L.jpg linked from the verified sngpl.com.pk Transmission System page) at full resolution around the Kohat/Attock/Dhulian cluster. concerns.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt this run (per scope note) and has zero Wayback snapshots (checked both the direct availability API and a CDX search -- no captures exist), so there is nothing of the sheet's own sourcing to re-verify; this is genuinely new research, not re-verification. wiki_citations.json has no entry for P4175, confirming the harvest never got in. It quotes an SNGPL officer (Hasham Khan) stating SNGPL 'linked Mansehra with 12 inches diameter pipeline' that was 'linked with mega supply line in Abbottabad,' bringing gas relief to Mansehra's CNG/commercial/domestic consumers. This independently confirms: (1) the pipeline is real, physically built infrastructure, not a database phantom; (2) SNGPL is the operator/owner, matching GEM's Owner1; (3) a Haripur-Abbottabad-Mansehra gas corridor exists and functions, consistent with GEM's Haripur->Mansehra routing (Haripur sits just north of Wah/Taxila on the way to Abbottabad and then Mansehra along the Hazara/KKH corridor -- straight-line driving distance Haripur-Mansehra is ~64 km per generic distance sites, plausibly close to the pipeline's stated 70.53 km once road/valley routing is accounted for). A second Wayback-archived URL from the same paper (print/277849) turned out to be the identical wire text republished under a different print ID, not an independent second source, so I am NOT double-counting it -- tier is medium (one strong, clearly independent source), not high. Could not find a second, distinct independent source after extensive searching (SNGPL annual report 2023 PDF text-searched for 'Haripur'/'Mansehra' -- only address-book hits for the Abbottabad regional office, no segment-level pipeline table; OGRA's site 403'd; two SNGPL tender PDFs referencing Abbottabad-region ditching work near Mansehra Road were located via search but failed url_verifier (200 but the expected 'Mansehra'/'Abbottabad' text was not extractable from the PDF, likely an image/scanned tender notice) so they are NOT cited; DuckDuckGo HTML search got rate-limited/CAPTCHA'd partway through, capping further attempts). CLASSIFICATION: transmission is consistent with how the dataset treats every other short (50-100 km, 8-24in) city-linking segment in this same Hazara/KP batch (P4176-P4182, P5486), so this is not a P4175-specific misclassification -- it is the dataset's convention for these trunk-to-city feeders, and the 2018 article's own language ('mega supply line') supports transmission-grade infrastructure rather than a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 63-pipeline roster -- no other row names Haripur or Mansehra, and the nearest geographic analogues (Wah-Nowshera I/II P4170/P4173, Rawat-Murree P4165, Dakhni-Meyal-Dhulian P4163) run west toward Peshawar or south toward Rawalpindi, not north into the Hazara corridor -- no plausible duplicate/relabel identified. SPEC (Length): 70.53 km is geographically plausible (see distance note above) but no independent source gives an exact km figure, so it remains unconfirmed rather than verified -- left as UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a ref. Net: existence, operator, and status are corroborated; the diameter figure is the one genuine open question, hence concern_type=spec rather than existence/duplicate/classification.

status_changes.researcher_notes: The recorded Status='construction' (LastUpdated 2025-07-11) is stale and, on the evidence, was probably never really accurate for the Pakistani side. Timeline: Feb/Mar 2024 — Pakistan's CCoE approved building an 80km border-to-Gwadar segment ($158m) purely to avoid an Iranian breach claim, but land in Gwadar was never acquired and no construction followed (Dawn, world-energy.org, both Feb 2024). Nov 2024 — Iran filed an $18bn arbitration claim at the Paris ICC over Pakistan's non-construction (multiple outlets). Jan 2026 — three independent Pakistani/trade outlets, all url_verifier-confirmed, report Pakistan formally notifying Iran it intends to place the project on hold and pursue an out-of-court settlement to abandon it (digitalpakistan.pk, Jan 14 2026: 'Pakistan has formally conveyed to Iran that it intends to place the Iran-Pakistan (IP) gas pipeline project on hold'; pipeline-journal.net, Jan 15 2026: 'Pakistan has notified Iran of its intention to abandon the long-stalled Iran-Pakistan (IP) gas pipeline project through an out-of-court settlement'), while a parallel legal track (thenews.pk, Jan 23 2026) has Pakistan simultaneously requesting a 10-year extension to 2035 to avoid the $18bn arbitration penalty, with a verdict expected 2027-28 if no settlement is reached — i.e. Pakistan is hedging between abandonment and a decade-long extension, but under NEITHER track is actual construction proceeding. Both the 'abandon via settlement' and the '10-year extension' framings describe a project that is on the shelf, not under construction, so I'm proposing Status=shelved (ShelvedCancelledType=Confirmed, since this is an explicitly reported decision, not the mechanical dormancy rule) rather than 'cancelled' (Pakistan has explicitly left revival on the table, contingent on a US sanctions waiver) or 'proposed' (there IS an existing signed agreement and a built Iranian half, so 'proposed' understates it). NEWER, non-decisive signal: by April-June 2026, several outlets (Pakistan Today Apr 11 2026, ProPakistani, Express Tribune, Global Connectivities Jun 2026) report 'revival hopes rise' after US-Iran peace talks/an Islamabad-mediated ceasefire process, with an unnamed expert saying a sanctions rollback 'could create room to restart work' — but this is speculative/conditional language, not a report of construction actually resuming, so it does not change my verdict; it does mean this determination should be re-checked again soon given how fluid the situation is. [QC] ShelvedCancelledType 'Confirmed' -> 'confirmed' (live-column vocab).

Timeline found: PITCO feasibility study for the Bahria Foundation LNG Terminal Project (Jul 2015-Mar 2017); ECC approval of the ISGS pipeline construction request (30 May 2018), reported by The Nation (19 Jun 2018); Exponent Engineers FEED review dated May 2018; Zameen News still describing the terminal as at the ECC-consideration stage in Mar 2019 (the most recent dated, independently-verifiable evidence I could find). I searched extensively (English and Urdu) for any 2020-2026 news on the Bahria Foundation Sonmiani LNG terminal or its Sonmiani-Nawabshah/Hub-Nawabshah pipeline -- found nothing: no completion, construction-start, cancellation, or revival story, and no mention in any of the Gwadar-Nawabshah-project revival coverage (that is a separate, unrelated project). ISGS's own site (isgs.com.pk) is Cloudflare-blocked to both WebFetch and curl; its Wayback Machine captures for the relevant project-gallery pages only preserved the site's homepage shell, not gallery content, so I could not check ISGS's own current project list. Engineering-firm portfolio pages (Exponent, PITCO) describing 'FEED completed'/'under development' are undated relative to today and read as legacy 2018-era project descriptions, not current updates. Given the current recorded Status is already 'shelved' and there is no independent evidence of any activity in roughly 7 years (since the 2019 evidence), this satisfies the 'shelved >=4y -> cancelled' dormancy rule. Presumed inference only -- no fabricated ref, per standing rule 2. [QC] ShelvedCancelledType 'Presumed' -> 'inferred' (live-column vocab).

Timeline of real progress: Jun-2018 MOU -> Feb-2019 inter-corporate agreement -> Gazprom's feasibility study originally slated to START Q1-2020 and finish within one year (Gulf Times). No source anywhere reports feasibility-study results, a financing close, or any construction milestone for THIS specific offshore/undersea project. The most recent substantive mention found is Warsaw Institute, 30-Sep-2022, which says only that 'a sea link between the offshore pipeline and the Pakistan Stream gas pipeline is now being considered' -- i.e. still speculative, no progress. A Feb-2023 Pipeline Technology Journal piece on reviving the North-South/Pakistan Stream project via Gwadar mentions an 'abandoned Gwadar LNG Pipeline Project' connecting to Iran, run by ISGS + Chinese firms -- this appears to be a RELATED BUT DISTINCT entity (an LNG-import + onshore pipe concept, not clearly the same as Gazprom's $10bn undersea line), so I have not merged it in, but it reinforces that the broader 'Gwadar seaborne gas import' concept had stalled by 2023. Broader Pakistan-Russia energy news through 2024-2025 (e.g. Gazprom/Novatek LNG talks, Portovaya/Ust-Luga LNG cooperation) has shifted entirely to LNG supply rather than this pipeline, with no mention of the offshore line being revived. Iran's own onshore IP pipeline (P0452) was separately reported abandoned by Pakistan in Aug-2023 over US-sanctions risk (Middle East Monitor), removing much of the rationale for an Iran-sourced offshore alternative too. With no independent evidence of activity since ~Sep-2022 (roughly 4 years dormant as of Aug-2026), the 2-year proposed-with-no-progress dormancy rule applies: propose Status=shelved, ShelvedCancelledType=Presumed, no fabricated ref per standing rule 2. [QC] ShelvedCancelledType 'Presumed' -> 'inferred' (live-column vocab).

Recorded Status='construction' with StartYear1=2025 (i.e. a still-future start) does not survive a check against SNGPL's own current corporate reporting. SNGPL's FY2025 Annual Report puts the near-identical project (16"-42" dia x 762km 'Qadirpur-Lahore Pipeline' + 25,000HP compression, 'gas downstream Sawan up to Lahore') on its p.76 'Milestones' page — a page of completed historical achievements (confirmed by TOC entry '76 Milestones' and by every neighboring entry being past-tense: Phase II 'was undertaken to transport additional 400 MMCFD RLNG downstream Sawan', Phase IV 'was laid for supply of RLNG to Power Plants i.e. Bhikki, Balloki, Haveli Bahadur Shah and Nandipur'). That Phase IV entry names the exact four RLNG power plants this trunk feeds. Independently, nsenergybusiness.com's Bhikki project page confirms the plant draws RLNG via an 18km spur off 'SNGPL's Qilla Sattar Shah to Bhikki pipeline' — Qilla Sattar Shah being the precise near-Lahore terminus named in the original 2017 sanction reporting for THIS pipeline (offshore-energy.biz: '42-inch pipeline from Sawan to Qilla Satar Shah, near Lahore, 780km'). And Dawn (Nov 2017) reports LNG-terminal-maintenance supply curtailments actually being applied to Bhikki/Balloki/Haveli Bahadur Shah/Nandipur with specific MMCFD figures — i.e. gas was demonstrably flowing to these plants via this network by November 2017. Three independent sources (SNGPL itself, an industry trade outlet, a national newspaper), none tracing to GEM or to each other, converge on: this trunk was built and moving RLNG by 2017, not merely 'under construction' toward a 2025 start that has by now already passed without incident in any source I found. I'm proposing StartYear1=2017 as the best-evidenced anchor (Dawn's Nov-2017 evidence of active flow) rather than a precise commissioning month, which I could not pin down further; a human should ideally cross-check against SNGPL's earlier (e.g. FY2017-18) annual report for an exact commissioning date/month before finalizing. Tier=high on the strength of three independent, differently-sourced confirmations; residual uncertainty is only about the EXACT month of the status change, not the direction of it. Did not attempt a staleness-rule demotion (the dormancy rules in the SOP apply to proposed/shelved decay, not to this situation, which is a positive-evidence upgrade, not a decay inference).

3,884.60 MMcf/d = 110 million cubic meters/day exactly. gulfoilandgas.com: 'The pipeline can carry 110 million cubic meters of gas a day' (50 mcm/d to Iran domestic use, 60 mcm/d to Pakistan). wsws.org (2008, citing a National Iranian Gas Company official): 'approximately 110 million cubic meters per day' (50 mcm/d Pakistan requirement + 60 mcm/d surplus). This total design-capacity figure matches GEM exactly and is corroborated by 2 independent sources -- initially I could not reconcile it against other sources' narrower Pakistan/India-allocation figures (60-90-150 mmscmd across different negotiation phases), but those describe country allocations, not total pipeline throughput; the 110 mcm/d total figure is the one that matches.
